QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_66

question.text: A fixed-coupon bond has a modified duration of 5 years. If market interest rates increase by 1% (100 basis points), by approximately how much does the bond's price change (first-order approximation, ignoring convexity)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Modified duration provides the first-order price sensitivity of a bond to a parallel change in yield: %ΔPrice ≈ −Modified Duration × ΔY. For a modified duration of 5 years and a yield increase of 1% (Δy = 0.01), the approximate price change is −5 × 0.01 = −5%, i.e., a 5% fall in price. Bond prices and yields move inversely. The Trap: Selecting "increases 5%" inverts the direction of the bond-price/yield relationship. "Unchanged" ignores rate sensitivity. "Increases 1%" confuses the rate change with the price change. Note: The XIX-A workbook covers YTM, FIRR, ROI, and MIRR. It does not explicitly state the modified-duration price-sensitivity formula. Treat duration-based price sensitivity as general fixed-income theory; deeper coverage is in NISM Series IV (Interest Rates Derivatives).
